ORDER This writ petition has been filed seeking direction to respondents 1 to 3 to pay compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- together with interest at the rate of 12% per annum.
2. The petitioner got married one, Shanthi on 06.06.2019.
Due to her illness, she was taken by the petitioner to Askar Clinic situated at Door No.7/2, Subrayan 4th Street, Otteri, Chennai at about 11.30 a.m.

While they were standing in front of the said clinic, a spark emanated from a pit which was dug up by the third respondent's contractor wherein underground storm water drainage work was also completed in which https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis dug up small hole to drain the rain water.
On account of the same, the petitioner and his wife got electrocuted due to which there was fire.
Fortunately, the petitioner fell down and his wife's cloth got fire and engulfed her entire body.

Immediately, she was taken to Kilpauk Medical College Hospital with the help of jurisdictional police i.e. the Inspector of Police, G5 Secretariat Colony Police Station and she was admitted as in-patient.
Immediately, the petitioner lodged complaint and the same was registered in crime No.273 of 2019 under accidental fire.
Unfortunately, she died on 30.08.2019.
After completion of investigation, post mortem certificate was issued by he Kilpauk Medical College Hospital stating that the petitioner's wife died of complication of burns-septicemia.
The accident had taken place only due to the negligent act on the part of the third respondent.

After completion of investigation,
the fourth respondent also filed final report on 12.01.2023 before the II Metropolitan Magistrate,
Egmore and the same has been taken cognizance in CC.No.1571 of 2023 for the offence punishable under Section 304A of IPC as against the contractors of the third respondent.
It is pending for trial.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 3.
Admittedly, the third respondent awarded contract to its contractor to lay storm water drainage.
After completion of the entire project, again in order to drain water, which was stagntated in the road, the contractor of the third respondent dug up holes in order to drain rain water.
While digging up a hole, they damaged the electric cable which was laid under the road, due to which there was fire accident.
Unfortunately, the petitioner and his wife got fire injuries.
Immediately, the petitioner fell down and he did not suffer from any fire injury.
However, his wife suffered with fire injuries on her whole body, due to which she died in the hospital.

4. The first respondent filed counter stating that the first respondent is not liable for any fire A.Raja vs The Chairman on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113426727/
2 accident where the underground electric lines were laid long back and the Chennai Corporation during the rain water system sewerage work, has not taken proper caution and due to that negligent act, has caused certain damage to the electric lines due to which there emanated spark.

That apart,
without any prior intimation https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis and permission, the third respondent directed its contractor to perform the said work.
The first respondent came to knowledge about the accident only after registration of FIR.
5. The second respondent filed counter stating that the second respondent had not carried out any underground drainage work at the place of accident.
Further stated that they laid sewerage main line in the middle of the road.
The machine holes are provided on the middle of the road.
Whereas the rain water drain canal is passing before the place of accident.
Therefore, the second respondent is not at all liable to pay any compensation as claimed by the petitioner.

6. The third respondent filed counter stating that since the accident occurred due to the burst of the electric cable maintained by the Tamilnadu Electricity Board, the petitioner has to approach the same for payment of compensation amount.
As such, there cannot be any presumption of negligence on the part of the third respondent.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 7

. As stated supra, the fourth respondent filed final report and the same has been taken cognizance in CC.No.1571 of 2023 on the file of the II Metropolitan Magistrate, Egmore, Chennai in which contractors of the third respondent are arrayed as accused.

Thus it is clear that only on the negligence on the part of the third respondent's contractor, the accident took place, due to which the petitioner's wife died.
It is also seen that she got married only on 06.06.2019.
Within a period of two months from the date of her marriage, she died due to the accident caused on the negligence of the third respondent's contractor.
Therefore, the third respondent is liable to pay compensation.
Hence, it should be compensated by means of monetary benefits by the third respondent.
The petitioner is being the legal heir of the deceased, entitled to receive just and fair compensation.
In respect of awarding compensation, there is no codified law for https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis arriving at quantum of compensation in these types of cases.
Therefore, the law such as Motor Vehicles Act and Workmen's Compensation Act may be applied for arriving at a just and fair compensation.
Further, the principles of absolute liability will have to be applied for these types of cases.

9. However, the learned Standing Counsel appearing for the third respondent would submit that it is a disputed question of facts and as such, it cannot be decided under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.
It is true that when disputed question of facts arises and if there is clear denial of tortious liability, remedy under Article 226 of the Constitution may not be proper.
But, it cannot be understood as laying a law that in every case of tortious liability recourse must be had to a suit.
When there is negligence on the face of it and infringement of Article 21 is there, it cannot be said that there will be any bar to proceed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.

Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for reasonable compensation from the third respondent for the death of the deceased and in the interest of justice, this Court would be https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis justified in considering the relief prayed by the petitioner.
The public law proceedings serve a different purpose than the private law proceedings.

The relief of monetary compensation, as exemplary damages, in proceedings under Article 32 by the Supreme Court or under Article 226 by the High Courts, for established infringement of the indefeasible right guaranteed under Article 21 is a remedy available in public law and is based on the strict liability for contravention of the guaranteed basic and indefeasible rights of the citizen.
10. The purpose of public law is not only to civilize public power but also to assure the citizen that they live under a legal system which aims to protect their interests and preserve their rights.

Therefore, when the court moulds the relief by granting 'compensation' in proceedings under Article 32 or 226 seeking enforcement or protection of fundamental rights, it does so under the public law by way of penalizing the wrongdoer and fixing the liability for the public wrong on the State which has failed in its public duty to protect the fundamental rights of the citizen.

The payment of compensation in such cases is not to https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis be understood, as it is generally understood in a civil action for damages under the private law but in the broader sense of providing relief by an order of making 'monetary amends' under the public law for the wrong done due to breach of public duty, of not protecting the fundamental rights of the citizen.

The compensation is in the nature of 'exemplary damages' awarded against the wrongdoer for the breach of its public law duty and is independent of the rights available to the aggrieved party to claim A.Raja vs The Chairman on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113426727/
4 compensation under the private law in an action based on tort, through a suit instituted in a court of competent jurisdiction or/and prosecute the offender under the penal law."
11.

In fact, the court is duty-bound and entitled to award 'just compensation'

the Court held as under: (Kant LJ p. 415) '9.
As a result of the amputation, the claimant had been rendered a cripple.

sentences.text: Accordingly, the 16 multiplier scale to be adopted to calculate the income of the deceased.
The petitioner's wife had been a housewife.
She died due to the accident occurred immediately after two months from the date of her marriage.
According to the petitioner, he is working as Security in a private hospital and his wife had also been a daily wage employee.
At the time of her death, she was aged about 35 years.
Though the petitioner failed to produce any proof for her income, her income notionally is fixed at Rs.15,000/- per month, in which 1/3 to be deducted for her personal expenses.
Hence, the monthly income to be fixed for calculating the compensation as Rs.10,000/- per month.

Accordingly, the total compensation is arrived at as follows:
 Total income Rs.10000/- p.m. x 12 x 16  =Rs.19,20,000/-
 Transport Expenses Rs.10,000/-
 Funeral Expenses Rs.25,000/-
 Loss of Consortium Rs.2,00,000/-
 Loss of Love and Affection Rs.3,00,000/-
 Total Rs.24,55,000/-
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 14.
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled to compensation to the tune of Rs.24,55,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the accident i.e. 30.08.2019 till payment.
The third respondent shall pay the said compensation within a period of twelve weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
15. With the above direction, this writ petition stands allowed.
There shall be no order as to costs.
